headline: South Asia: Syria weighing whether to join Makkah pact: foreign minister
script:
Good morning. This is your global conflict briefing.

BOTTOM LINE UP FRONT:
- South Asia: Syria weighing whether to join Makkah pact: foreign minister.
- Western Russia: Ukraine strikes Russian rocket fuel plant with Neptune missiles and drones – General Staff.
- Persian Gulf Region: New Saudi luxury airline forced to cancel, redivert flights under Houthi attacks - report.

Full breakdown follows.

NORTH AMERICA
United States - bottom line: Low-altitude Air Force One Halloween flyover rattles DC residents.
- Military Times, 21 hours ago: Low-altitude Air Force One Halloween flyover rattles DC residents.
During a White House Halloween celebration, trick-or-treaters and D.C. residents were surprised with a flyover that left some unsettled by its low altitude and only 15-minute warning.
Central America: no notable developments in the last 48 hours.
The Caribbean: no notable developments in the last 48 hours.

SOUTH AMERICA
South America: no notable developments in the last 48 hours.

EUROPE
Western Russia - bottom line: Ukraine strikes Russian rocket fuel plant with Neptune missiles and drones – General Staff.
- Ukrainska Pravda, The Hindu - International, 5 hours ago: Ukraine strikes Russian rocket fuel plant with Neptune missiles and drones – General Staff.
Ukrainian forces have struck the Kamensky Plant in Russia's Rostov Oblast with Neptune missiles and drones, damaging four production workshops.
- Ukrainska Pravda, 6 hours ago: Russia strikes Dnipropetrovsk Oblast energy facilities again, leaving residents without power.
Russian attacks on the night of 30-31 October severely damaged energy equipment in Dnipropetrovsk Oblast, including two facilities belonging to DTEK Dnipro Power Grids.
- Ukrainska Pravda, 6 hours ago: Russian attacks on Donetsk and Kharkiv oblasts kill two and injure 23.
Two people, including a 16-year-old boy, were killed and 23 others injured in Russian attacks on Donetsk and Kharkiv oblasts on 30 October. In addition, 12 people in Kharkiv Oblast were suffering from shock.
- Ukrainska Pravda, 6 hours ago: She shielded her son and daughter with her body: mother of two killed in Russian attack on Kremenchuk.
A mother of two known only as Anna was killed in Russia's attack on Kremenchuk on 29 October. Anna did not have time to reach a safe place before the attack, but she shielded her daughter Kseniia and son Yehor with her body.
Southern Europe - bottom line: Tusk-Nawrocki battle escalates as chief judge is ousted from Poland’s top court.
- Politico Europe, 19 hours ago: Tusk-Nawrocki battle escalates as chief judge is ousted from Poland’s top court.
A bid to remove the court’s nationalist-linked leadership sparked accusations of a coup and clashes between protesters and police in Warsaw.
- Politico Europe, 5 hours ago: Zelenskyy urges US to speed up Patriot deliveries.
Washington approved the sale of 500 interceptors to counter Russian ballistic missile attacks.

AFRICA
Persian Gulf Region - bottom line: New Saudi luxury airline forced to cancel, redivert flights under Houthi attacks - report.
- Jerusalem Post, 4 hours ago: New Saudi luxury airline forced to cancel, redivert flights under Houthi attacks - report.
Riyadh Air staff started volunteering at hospitals where victims of the airport strikes were treated as flights were canceled and redirected, and the airline moved its expensive assets from Riyadh.
- Jerusalem Post, 22 hours ago: IDF kills Hamas commander involved in holding Noa Argamani, 11 other hostages.
The IDF said the two terrorists had advanced attacks against Israeli troops and civilians throughout the war, and worked to restore Hamas's military capabilities.
- Jerusalem Post, one hour ago: Israel prepares for possible Iran escalation as US delays military action until after midterms.
Israeli officials assess that Iran is stalling nuclear talks as Washington weighs military action, while the IDF prepares for a possible Gaza City offensive.
- Al Jazeera - Middle East, 4 hours ago: Iran warns of unfettered retaliation if attacked as mediators try for peace.
Iran’s supreme leader says Tehran’s potential response will not be restricted by geography.
Africa - bottom line: Drone strikes in Ethiopia kill at least 25: witnesses.
- Africanews, 7 hours ago: Drone strikes in Ethiopia kill at least 25: witnesses.
Multiple drone strikes have hit northern regions of Ethiopia since Thursday, killing at least 25 civilians, including children, witnesses and a medical source said on Friday
- Africanews, 23 hours ago: President Ruto seeks compensation for Kenyans recruited into Russian military.
An investigation by Journalists for Justice, published earlier this month, identified at least 76 Kenyans killed while fighting for Russia, alongside 841 Kenyan nationals recruited between October 2022 and June 2026.
- Africanews, 8 hours ago: Ghana in talks with Russia for first nuclear power plant.
Russian President Vladimir Putin met his Ghanaian counterpart John Dramani Mahama for bilateral talks the next day after Russia-Africa summit in Moscow
- AllAfrica - Conflict, 20 hours ago: Nigeria: How to Prevent Another Attack in Taraba Beyond Security Deployment.
[Daily Trust] The latest attack on Binnari community in Karim-Lamido Local Government Area of Taraba State has left dozens dead, homes destroyed and residents fearful of another possible attack. Despite previous security measures in the area, the incident has renewed concerns about how vulnerable communities can be better protected.
South Africa - bottom line: Malawi: Police Confirm Egyptian Deputy Ambassador Beaten in Lilongwe Attack.
- AllAfrica - Southern Africa, one day ago: Malawi: Police Confirm Egyptian Deputy Ambassador Beaten in Lilongwe Attack.
[Nyasa Times] A senior Egyptian diplomat has been hospitalised after being attacked and beaten in Lilongwe, sparking a police investigation into the shocking assault.

ASIA
South Asia - bottom line: Syria weighing whether to join Makkah pact: foreign minister.
- Dawn (Pakistan), 4 hours ago: Syria weighing whether to join Makkah pact: foreign minister.
Syria’s Foreign Minister Asaad al-Shaibani on Saturday said Damascus was considering whether to join the Makkah defence pact that binds Pakistan, Saudi Arabia and Turkiye. The Makkah Joint Defence Agreement, signed on Aug 7, empowers the three members to consider an armed attack on one member an attack on all. “Discussions are currently underway to evaluate Syria’s entry into the Makkah alliance,” Al Shaibani said at the Manama Dialogue conference in Bahrain.
- Dawn (Pakistan), South China Morning Post - China, The Hindu - International, 2 hours ago: Iran's supreme leader warns US, Israel of 'unrestricted geographical response' to new attacks.
Iran’s Supreme Leader Mojtaba Khamenei on Saturday warned the United States and Israel against returning to war, according to a written statement, following threats from the Islamic republic’s foes of a possible resumption of strikes. “If the enemies once again launch military or terrorist attacks, it is the armed forces of the Islamic Republic and the Iranian nation that will determine the time and conditions for ending them,” said a statement attributed to Khamenei posted on his website.
- Dawn (Pakistan), 14 hours ago: KP police get tech to monitor counterterrorism operations.
PESHAWAR: The Khyber Pakhtunkhwa police have integrated anti-drone systems and surveillance drones operating across the province into the Safe City Peshawar’s Command and Control Centre to strengthen security and surveillance capabilities. With the integration of Safe City cameras and anti-drone systems, live video and surveillance feeds from police drones operating anywhere in the province, including during field operations and offensives carried out against terrorists by the police and the Counter Terrorism Department (CTD), can now be monitored at the Command and Control Centre.
- Dawn (Pakistan), 2 hours ago: Mansehra assistant commissioner injured as vehicle comes under attack in Nowshera.
PESHAWAR: Mansehra Assistant Commissioner (AC) Adil Waseem was injured on Saturday when unknown gunmen opened fire at his official vehicle in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa’s Nowshera district, officials said. Muhammad Asim, the spokesperson of Peshawar’s Lady Reading Hospital, said Waseem was “stable” and was receiving medical treatment. Waseem came under attack in Nowshera’s Panah Kot area while on his way back from his native village Saleh Khana in the district, police officials in Nowshera said. He sustained injuries and was immediately taken to the hospital.
Asia - bottom line: Kim Jong-un urges drone expansion as North Korea showcases new unmanned tech.
- South China Morning Post - China, 13 hours ago: Kim Jong-un urges drone expansion as North Korea showcases new unmanned tech.
North Korean leader Kim Jong-un attended an exhibition devoted to drones and called for rapidly expanding the country’s drone technology, state media reported on Friday, as his military escalates threats against South Korea and the United States. Acquiring advanced drones is a top priority for Kim, who now wants to strengthen conventional and nuclear capabilities to counter what he calls US-led security threats. It is unclear how far North Korea’s drone programme has progressed. Experts say...
- South China Morning Post - China, 4 hours ago: Is Beijing’s 2027 military milestone now a US readiness deadline over Taiwan?.
America’s push for 2027 combat readiness in the Indo-Pacific is raising questions over whether a year that US military officials linked to a possible People’s Liberation Army attack on Taiwan has instead become a planning benchmark. The preparations come despite a US intelligence assessment published in March that mainland Chinese leaders “do not currently plan” to attack Taiwan in 2027, “nor do they have a fixed timeline for achieving unification”. General Ronald Clark, commander of US Army...
- South China Morning Post - China, 14 hours ago: G20 talks expose deep rift as Russia stays defiant while Rubio pursues sideline diplomacy.
Russia showed no sign on Friday of softening its stance on Kyiv as G20 foreign ministers opened talks in the United States, with the Ukraine and Iran wars deepening rifts between the sprawling forum’s members. Sharp disagreements emerged around the table, with EU foreign policy chief Kaja Kallas accusing Russian Foreign Minister Sergey Lavrov of presenting “lies” on issues like the conflict in Ukraine. “He put forward a lot of lies, a lot of false narratives” that Europeans were able to push...
- South China Morning Post - China, one hour ago: DR Congo Ebola deaths top 5,000, cases recorded in other African nations.
Deaths in the Democratic Republic of Congo’s (DRC’s) Ebola outbreak have topped 5,000 as the country grapples with the relentless spread of the disease and cases are recorded in other African countries, the latest government data on Saturday shows. Data from the government’s Ministry of Health showed that the disease has killed 5,026 people out of 10,351 infected, at a nearly 50 per cent lethality rate. The surge is sparking concerns among experts regarding the authorities’ ability to contain...
India - bottom line: Kim Jong Un's cyber army: How North Korea's hackers steal billions for regime.
- Times of India - Top Stories, 2 hours ago: Kim Jong Un's cyber army: How North Korea's hackers steal billions for regime.
North Korea has developed a sophisticated cyberwar machine enabling it to target financial institutions worldwide. The country's state-sponsored hackers increasingly rely on social engineering and malware to infiltrate cryptocurrency companies. Cyber operations are essential for generating funds due to international sanctions and economic isolation. Reports suggest that North Korea has stolen billions in cryptocurrency through extensive cybercriminal activity. These actions directly support its military programs and other state priorities.
- Times of India - Top Stories, one hour ago: Georgia developer's 30% profit claim fails as court finds no partnership.
The business collaboration between Bruce Mortimer and Jeff White culminated in a legal clash centered on a software project. Jeff contended he was promised future profits and operational privileges. However, the Georgia Court of Appeals ruled that an enforceable partnership agreement was lacking due to vague terms. Consequently, White's claims regarding unpaid services and intellectual property were dismissed, highlighting the necessity of explicitly outlining business agreements.
- Times of India - Top Stories, 3 hours ago: IIT-Bombay suicide case: Sahil’s parents seek CBI probe, CCTV, witness protection.
Parents of Sahil Wakode, an IIT Bombay student who died by suicide, have petitioned for an independent investigation into his death. They allege that their son faced harassment and caste-based humiliation from a professor. The petition seeks to direct investigations towards actions by those in authority at the institute. They demand preservation of evidence and protection for potential witnesses.
- Times of India - Top Stories, 3 hours ago: Udupi man dies by suicide at govt hospital after being thrased by girlfriend's kin.
Pradeep, a 27-year-old man from Nairkodi, was assaulted by the family of his girlfriend after an alleged altercation. The incident occurred on October 27, when several of the girl's brothers attacked him, causing severe injuries. After being hospitalized due to the assault, Pradeep expressed his distress and received threats from the girl's family. On October 30, Pradeep was found to have died by suicide in the hospital's toilet.
Korean Peninsula: no notable developments in the last 24 hours.

AUSTRALIA
Australia - bottom line: Evacuees from Russian-occupied Oleshky reach Ukraine amid ceasefire.
- ABC News Australia, South China Morning Post - China, Al Jazeera - Middle East, one hour ago: Evacuees from Russian-occupied Oleshky reach Ukraine amid ceasefire.
Residents evacuated from the Russian-occupied city of Oleshky have reached Ukraine under the most significant truce since Russia's invasion of Ukraine in 2022.
- ABC News Australia, 3 hours ago: Iranian military ordered to counter any attack swiftly and without restraint.
Iran's military chiefs should meet any attack on its country with an immediate and unrestrained response, Supreme Leader Mjotaba Khamenei has ordered.
- ABC News Australia, 6 hours ago: Bodycam video shows ICE agent's car swerving toward man in Texas.
CCTV and body camera video shows the agent making sharp moves towards the man with his SUV as the man runs away.
- ABC News Australia, 8 hours ago: Australia slumps to horror defeat as Warner decries 'deplorable' batting.
Australia falls in a heap on day five of the third Test in Cape Town, spun out by Simon Harmer to lose the game by 176 runs and suffer a 2-1 series loss to South Africa.
